# Decision-conflict report

## Computed (declared-edge completeness)

(none)

## Judged (undeclared-conflict sweep)

- **judged-wall-canvas-v2-dc-1-vs-workbench-redesign-dc-10** [no-conflict]: Story dc-1 departs from the handoff design. The handoff replaces the uncovered coverage chip with the readiness mark; the story keeps the chip and draws the mark beside it. Parent dc-10 allows lower fidelity to the handoff only 'where these decisions differ', which means where the parent's own decisions differ. No parent decision covers this departure. The story bases it on parent ac-2 ('coverage chips with their existing texts'), so the tension sits mostly inside the parent, between ac-2 and dc-10. Still, the story declares a departure from the handoff without a parent decision or an edge carrying it. The fix is to name ac-2 as a fidelity exception in the parent, or to accept the reading explicitly. (confidence 0.22) — Parent ac-2, an acceptance criterion, requires the coverage chips with their existing texts; parent dc-10's fidelity to the handoff yields to the parent's own criteria, and story dc-1 names ac-2 as its basis. Carried unchanged from the accepted v1.
- **judged-wall-canvas-v2-dc-2-vs-workbench-redesign-dc-10** [no-conflict]: Story dc-2 also departs from the handoff. The handoff's type picker lists six edge types; the story offers only the legal subset and treats the six rows as styling only. Parent dc-10 holds the handoff's states and copy to high fidelity, with exceptions only where the parent's decisions differ. This departure rests on parent co-7, which is a constraint and not a decision, so it falls outside dc-10's stated exception. In substance, co-7 and ac-2 require this behaviour, so there is no real contradiction. The gap is in how dc-10's exception clause is worded. (confidence 0.12) — Offering only the legal edge types is required by parent co-7 and ac-2; a constraint binds more strongly than dc-10's fidelity decision, whose exception wording names decisions only by omission. Carried unchanged from the accepted v1.
- **judged-wall-canvas-v2-dc-1-readiness-mark-vs-workbench-redesign-dc-6** [no-conflict]: Story dc-1 adds a new chip to cards: a readiness mark, shown as a dot plus an 'unresolved' or 'no stub' chip, on a card that a Focus next concern names. It does not say whether this chip follows the card-badge contract that parent dc-6 keeps and restates: compact receipt-row chips; each badge element a button carrying data-badge-source and its serialized derivation record; three-valued, with a disclosed-unproven value drawn in the disclosure style. It also does not say what happens when stub declarations or readiness cannot be read. Parent dc-5 (an unreadable input is disclosed, never counted as zero coverage) and co-3 rule out showing 'no stub' in that case. Showing it would be a reading nobody declared against dc-6 and dc-5. The mark should state that it renders as a disclosure when its input is unreadable. (confidence 0.15) — The readiness mark is a card chip under parent dc-6's kept badge contract, and story co-1 binds parent co-3 (three-valued honesty) and dc-5: when its input (readiness or stub declarations) cannot be read, the mark renders a disclosure in the disclosure style, never 'no stub'. The F2 lane brief carries this. Carried unchanged from the accepted v1.
